issues.detail: Rule condition uses prev_in & ~in (any falling bit) but example expects full 0xFFFFFFFF capture from a single transition of all bits; condition is per-bit OR, not all-bits, so example is consistent only because all bits fall. However, the rule's condition text '(prev_in & ~in) != 0' implies any falling bit sets only those bits, while example shows all bits set when all fall—no contradiction there. Real issue: R2 example first row reset=0,in=all ones expects out=0, but if prev_in is uninitialized/unknown, behavior undefined; spec does not define initial prev_in. Also R2 visible=next_cycle but example row2 expects out=all ones at same row as falling edge—timing mismatch: if visible next_cycle, row2 (in=0) should show out=0 and row3 show all ones. Example contradicts visible field.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next

issues.detail: R2 example: vectors row1 in=0xFFFFFFFF, row2 in=0, expected row2 out=0xFFFFFFFF. With visible=next_cycle, output should appear one cycle after the falling edge, i.e., row3, not row2. Example contradicts rule's visible timing.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next

issues.detail: R3 example never has a prior capture, so out stays 0; it does not test hold after a 1 is captured. The rule claims hold until reset, but example only shows no-capture hold. Not contradictory but weak grounding.
issues.spec_evidence: the output will remain 1 until the register is reset

issues.detail: R1 example row1 reset=1,in=all ones expected out=0; row2 reset=1,in=0 expected out=0; row3 reset=0,in=0 expected out=0. This does not test that reset clears a previously captured 1. Also reset is synchronous; example does not show reset asserted after capture.
issues.spec_evidence: until the register is reset (active high synchronous reset)

issues.detail: Spec says capture when input changes 1->0; contract uses prev_in & ~in (any falling bit) and sets only those bits. Alternative semantics: capture sets all 32 output bits to 1 if any bit falls (sticky global flag). Distinguishing sequence: row1 reset=0,in=0x00000001; row2 reset=0,in=0x00000000. Per-bit semantics yields out=0x00000001; global-any semantics yields out=0xFFFFFFFF.
issues.spec_evidence: For each bit in a 32-bit vector, capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next.
issues.alternative: Any falling bit sets all 32 output bits to 1 (global sticky flag).

issues.detail: Initial value of prev_in / out_reg at time 0 is unspecified. Alternative: prev_in initialized to 0 vs all ones vs unknown. Distinguishing sequence: first row reset=0,in=0. If prev_in=0, no capture, out=0; if prev_in=all ones, capture all bits, out=0xFFFFFFFF (next cycle).
issues.alternative: prev_in initialized to all ones at time 0, causing a capture on first row if in=0.

issues.detail: Rule condition uses bitwise prev_in & ~in != 0, but spec says 'for each bit' capture when that bit changes 1->0. The condition is correct for per-bit but the rule does not explicitly state that only falling bits are set, not all bits. Example with all bits falling masks this. Missing verbatim evidence for per-bit set behavior.
issues.spec_evidence: For each bit in a 32-bit vector, capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next.

issues.detail: Derived outputs for R2 example under contract semantics (visible next_cycle): row1 in=all ones, out=0; row2 in=0, falling edge, out should still be 0 (next_cycle); row3 out=all ones; row4 out=all ones. Contract example expects row2 out=all ones, contradicting visible=next_cycle. Under same_cycle semantics, row2 out=all ones would be correct. Inconsistency between visible field and example.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next
